scope: Bounded independent legal-scope peer review: purchased personal Japan-posted 100 g factory-sealed manufactured steamed/rolled/dried Camellia sinensis sencha; no permits, certificates, special registration or agency advance notice. Ordinary customs declarations and arrival inspection allowed.

exactProvisions: Invoeringswet openbare lichamen Bonaire, Sint Eustatius en Saba 18.2.4a–b
findings.reasoning: The plant-product definition and delegated power do not themselves publish the operative commodity conditions for all three islands. The food-law household exception concerns food manufactured within the private household, not purchased imported food. Its powers to regulate imports and registration are not an unqualified certificate duty. Bonaire’s dried-herb allowance in the Venezuela reopening notice has both an origin and an island limit.
findings.remainingConflict: The applicable island-specific delegated import rules and their processing scope for Japan-origin manufactured sencha are not established; neither a country-code-wide exemption nor an enacted universal certificate requirement follows.
findings.targetedNewLeadResult: A narrow search for the operative BES plant-disease rules did not yield the missing instrument; results concerned unrelated pesticides or other laws. Government law-site access also encountered robots restrictions. These negative results were not treated as proof of exemption.

exactProvisions: Food Safety and Quality Act 2016 sections 1(2), 2, 4, 35(1)–(2), 54
findings.reasoning: The plant-permit HS list omits 0902, but cannot by itself waive a separate food duty. Section 35 is broad in isolation; section 4 expressly applies the Act to food businesses. Broad food-business/importer definitions and the foreign store’s sale do not settle application to a private consignee. Section 35(2) is a discretionary relaxation, not an automatic personal-post exemption. Ordinary sealed packaging is not necessarily aseptic sealing.
findings.remainingConflict: Commencement and actual application of the food-import provisions to purchased personal post remain unestablished. It would be unsound either to exclude solely by section 35 while ignoring section 4, or to infer a universal private-import exemption.
findings.targetedNewLeadResult: Re-read full saved Act definitions and operative sections. Exact official personal-tea query yielded no material new rule; direct food-conditions page access failed. Prior current-law and schedule searches were not repeated.

findings.reasoning: Household food manufacture is exempted, but that does not itself cover purchased imports. The general food statute empowers implementing import rules rather than imposing an immediate foreign certificate. Customs plants/flowers controls and traveler guidance do not classify manufactured sencha.
findings.remainingConflict: No operative LVV commodity or processing rule has been established for finished Japan-origin personal postal tea.
findings.targetedNewLeadResult: The specific plant-disease implementing-law lead returned the Pesticides Ordinance and unrelated local rules, not a commodity import rule. Exact NVWA tea lead did not resolve scope. These were rejected as irrelevant, not used as negative legal proof.

exactProvisions: Landsbesluit publieke gezondheid AB 2017 no. 33 article 4(2)–(3), explanatory notes
findings.reasoning: The food notification duty is expressly commercial-use-only; the health certificate categories do not include plain tea. Quantity/presentation, rather than the fact that a purchase was paid, governs the personal/commercial distinction in the official notes. This closes the independent food-document issue for the proposed personal quantity but not the separate agricultural one.
findings.remainingConflict: The outstanding issue is the actual LVV plant-product classification or import conditions for manufactured tea; an individual ruling is not intrinsically necessary if a published rule can settle it.
findings.targetedNewLeadResult: A precise primary-law search returned conservation/CITES law and the underlying Public Health Act. Neither supplies the missing finished-food agricultural processing rule; no speculative conservation prohibition was applied.

exactProvisions: Official law index as at 1 January 2026: Plant Protection Ordinance Cap. 93, Plant Protection Regulations amended SI 35/2002, Prohibition of Importation of Plants Regulations SI 13/1996 as amended
Virgin Islands Food Security and Sustainability Act 2/2022: indexed not in force
findings.reasoning: The current official index identifies operative older plant instruments and amendments. The newer 2022 law is expressly not in force, so cannot replace their missing conditions. Nursery-oriented import guidance cannot safely classify dried retail tea.
findings.remainingConflict: The full operative older regulations/commodity annexes and amendments remain unavailable in the examined official online law collection. A missing text is the impediment, not a substantive conclusion that tea requires individual permission.
findings.targetedNewLeadResult: Re-read the exact 2026 current-law entries and preserved the prior five-page official revised-law collection search. No fresh generic query was made after that specific primary-source lead was exhausted.

exactProvisions: Tristan Island Council Ordinance section 15(1), 15(5), Schedule 3(f)
Tristan Biosecurity Ordinance 2021: government consolidated headnote not yet in force
St Helena Food Hygiene Regulations regulation 4(4) as potentially applied locally
findings.reasoning: St Helena and Ascension have separate favourable findings, but the country code also covers Tristan. Schedule 3(f) lists possible by-law subjects concerning potentially diseased living/dead plants and animals; section 15(1) authorizes making such by-laws. It is not itself an operative import prohibition or certificate requirement. Section 15(5) permits by-laws to commence through publication on the Administrator’s local notice board. The saved current online materials do not resolve a manufactured-tea rule or the 2021 ordinance commencement. Food-business notice rules were not transferred to a private consumer.
findings.remainingConflict: An operative Tristan rule or published scope interpretation covering the current live/dead-plant warning and manufactured tea remains missing. Local notice-board commencement means an online search alone cannot prove absence of applicable by-laws. Country-wide approval remains unsupported, without asserting a blanket tea prohibition.
findings.targetedNewLeadResult: Re-read the full saved local law, specifically section 15 and Schedule 3. This narrowed the significance of broad plant-control language to an enabling power and identified the local publication mechanism; it did not supply the missing operative tea condition.

conclusion: All six decisions remain unresolved. The persistent barriers are missing operative rules/text or a genuine scope conflict, not an assumption that every finished tea needs an individual authority ruling. No contacts made; no absence-of-search-result exemptions inferred.
